answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, non-refundable deposit that is slashed when peers prove misbehavior, like a black onyx seal pressed once per identity. Cheap copies then cost real money, while honest agents build a reputation lagoon, a shared pool of endorsements that deepens over time and cannot be faked overnight. A newcomer must first do useful, verifiable work, cracking the walnut of trust gradually, before it can vote or earn; identities that appear in swarms without history simply stay voiceless.
